question: An object has a weight of 24 N on Earth. What will be its weight on the Moon’s surface?
solution:
The correct answer is __**6 N**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **The weight of an object** is the force exerted on it due to gravity. It is calculated as **Weight = Mass × Gravitational acceleration (g).**
 
• The gravitational acceleration on the **Moon** is approximately **1/6th** of that on the **Earth** (Earth's g ≈ 9.8 m/s², Moon's g ≈ 1.63 m/s²).
 
• On Earth, the given weight of the object is **24 N.** Since weight is the product of mass and gravity, the mass of the object can be calculated using: **Mass = Weight / g (Earth).**
 
• Using the calculated mass, we can determine the weight on the Moon: **Weight on Moon = Mass × g (Moon).**
 
• After substituting the values, the object's weight on the Moon is found to be **6 N.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gravitational Acceleration:**

 
 
• The gravitational acceleration on the **Earth** is approximately **9.8 m/s².**
 
• The gravitational acceleration on the **Moon** is approximately **1.63 m/s².**
 
• This difference in gravity is due to the Moon's smaller **mass** and **radius** compared to the Earth.
 
 
 
• **Mass vs. Weight:**
 
 
• **Mass** is the measure of the amount of matter in an object and remains constant irrespective of location.
 
• **Weight** is the force exerted on an object due to gravity and changes based on the gravitational field strength.
 
 
 
• **Calculation Process:**
 
 
• Step 1: Determine the mass of the object on Earth:
 
 
• Mass = Weight / g (Earth) = 24 N / 9.8 m/s² ≈ 2.45 kg.
 
 
 
• Step 2: Calculate the weight on the Moon:
 
 
• Weight on Moon = Mass × g (Moon) = 2.45 kg × 1.63 m/s² ≈ 6 N.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Weight on Other Celestial Bodies:**
 
 
• An object's weight varies on different planets or celestial bodies due to variations in gravitational acceleration.
 
• For example, the gravity on **Mars** is about **3.71 m/s²,** while on **Jupiter**, it is approximately **24.79 m/s².**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Weight-to-Mass Ratio:** The weight of an object depends directly on its mass and the gravitational field of the celestial body it is on.
 
• **Moon's Gravity:** The Moon’s weaker gravity is a result of its smaller size and lower density compared to Earth.
 
• **Practical Applications:** Understanding weight differences on celestial bodies is crucial for space exploration and designing equipment for extraterrestrial environments.
 
• **Historical Missions:** This concept was a significant factor in planning lunar missions like the **Apollo program**, where astronauts experienced reduced weight on the Moon.
